mcqs.q: What was the rabies vaccination coverage among owned dogs in this Madagascar survey?
mcqs.e: Only about one third (34%) of owned dogs were vaccinated against rabies.

mcqs.q: What were the main owner-cited obstacles to dog rabies vaccination?
o: Vaccine safety fears and religious beliefs
Lack of vaccine supply and government bans
Limited finances and poor access to veterinary care
Belief that dogs cannot transmit rabies
mcqs.e: Owners cited limited financial resources and difficulty accessing veterinary services as the chief barriers.

mcqs.q: What did the authors conclude about the accessibility of dogs for preventive vaccination?
o: Most dogs were ownerless and unreachable
Most dogs were accessible through their owners
Vaccination should target only stray dogs
Vaccination is unnecessary given low rabies risk
mcqs.e: Most dogs were owned and thus reachable for vaccination, yet coverage remained low.

mcqs.q: What was the most common pathophysiologic cause of death in this feline necropsy series?
mcqs.e: Cancer was the leading pathophysiologic cause of death (35.81%), found in 41.3% of cats.

mcqs.q: How did reproductive status relate to feline lifespan?
o: Intact cats lived longer than altered cats
Intact cats had significantly shorter lifespans
mcqs.e: Intact females and males had significantly shorter lifespans than spayed/neutered cats.

mcqs.q: Which retrovirus status was associated with decreased longevity?
mcqs.e: FeLV-positive status reduced longevity, whereas FIV status was not associated with shorter lifespan.

mcqs.q: How did FeLV prevalence change across the three study periods in San Mateo feral cats?
mcqs.e: FeLV prevalence fell significantly from 1.73% to 0.29% (p=0.01).

mcqs.q: What sex pattern was seen for FIV positivity?
o: Significantly more positive males than females
Significantly more positive females than males
mcqs.e: Significantly more FIV-positive males than females were identified in each year and period.

mcqs.q: What did the authors conclude regarding retrovirus monitoring in these free-living cats?
o: Continued testing and surveillance is needed
Prevalence is too low to matter
mcqs.e: The findings supported continued FIV testing and surveillance among free-living cats.

mcqs.q: Which infectious agents were most important causes of ocular disease in these cats?
o: FeLV, FIP virus, and Cryptococcus sp.
mcqs.e: FeLV, feline infectious peritonitis virus, and Cryptococcus sp. were the leading infectious causes of ocular lesions.

mcqs.q: What was the most common ocular abnormality associated with infectious agents?
mcqs.e: Uveitis (anterior, posterior, or panuveitis) was the most common infection-associated ocular finding.

mcqs.q: What examination approach did the authors recommend for suspected infectious ocular disease?
o: Both gross and histologic evaluation of the eyes
mcqs.e: Because gross lesions are less common than histologic ones, both gross and histologic eye evaluation was recommended.

journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery

mcqs.q: Most cats with positive FeLV immunoassay but negative proviral PCR had what underlying condition?
o: Primary bone marrow disease or marrow insult
mcqs.e: Discordant cats mostly had primary bone marrow disease (largely autoimmune) or a marrow insult/systemic inflammation.

mcqs.q: What testing recommendation did the authors make for low-prevalence populations?
o: Confirm positive immunoassays with FeLV proviral DNA PCR
Treat all positives as truly infected
mcqs.e: Positive LFI/ELISA results in cats with marrow disease should be followed by proviral DNA PCR, especially where prevalence is low.

mcqs.q: What was the survival outcome of the discordant (immunoassay-positive, PCR-negative) cats?
mcqs.e: 85.7% survived to discharge, and most of those lived 4 months to 6 years.

mcqs.q: How did FIV and FeLV prevalence compare in this Brazilian semiarid cohort?
mcqs.e: FIV prevalence was 30.2% versus only 1.1% for FeLV.

mcqs.q: Which factor was significantly associated with FIV infection?
mcqs.e: Male sex carried a markedly elevated odds of FIV infection (OR 5.7).

mcqs.q: Which clinicopathologic change characterized FIV-positive cats?
o: Higher albumin and higher A:G ratio
Lower albumin and lower A:G ratio
mcqs.e: FIV-positive cats showed lower albumin and a reduced albumin:globulin ratio alongside higher globulins.

journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery

mcqs.q: How has global FIV prevalence changed since the virus was discovered ~40 years ago?
mcqs.e: Global FIV prevalence (~4.7%) stayed largely constant from 1980 to 2017.

mcqs.q: Which demographic showed higher FIV prevalence?
mcqs.e: Over 90% of studies reported greater prevalence in older male cats.

mcqs.q: What was the expert consensus on FIV vaccination?
o: Not typically recommended and discontinued in North America
mcqs.e: Experts agreed FIV vaccination is not typically recommended and has been discontinued in North America.

journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery

mcqs.q: How did anti-rabies antibody titres compare after concurrent versus separate FeLV/rabies booster vaccination?
mcqs.e: Titres did not differ significantly (P=0.141) and all cats reached the protective ≥0.5 IU/ml threshold.

mcqs.q: What did the study conclude about concurrent administration of the two vector vaccines?
o: It interferes with immunity and should be avoided
It is a better option than separate visits
It causes substantially more adverse events
mcqs.e: Concurrent administration did not impair immunity or raise adverse events, making it preferable to separate visits.

mcqs.q: What was the overall prognostic value of NLR, MLR, and PLR for survival in retrovirus-positive cats?
mcqs.e: The leukocyte ratios had very limited prognostic value for survival in retrovirus-positive cats.

mcqs.q: How did MLR in FeLV-antigen-positive cats compare to controls?
mcqs.e: MLR was significantly lower in FeLV-Ag-positive cats (0.05) than controls (0.14).

mcqs.q: How did most compounded famciclovir formulations perform on accuracy and precision?
mcqs.e: Most compounded formulations were inaccurate, imprecise, and inconsistent in drug content.

mcqs.q: What did the authors recommend for managing feline herpesvirus-1?
mcqs.e: FDA-approved tablets were accurate and preferred over compounded formulations.

mcqs.q: If compounding is used, which concentration was preferred?
mcqs.e: 250 mg/mL was preferred because the 400 mg/mL suspensions were markedly less accurate.

mcqs.q: What was the most frequent underlying cause of chronic upper respiratory signs in these cats?
mcqs.e: Neoplasia was the most frequent finding, followed by rhinitis and anatomical defects.

mcqs.q: Which bacterial genus predominated in feline chronic rhinitis isolates?
mcqs.e: Pseudomonas species was the main bacterial isolate identified.

mcqs.q: Given the resistance findings, what did the authors advise regarding antimicrobials?
o: Use only the most expensive agents
mcqs.e: The resistance pattern prompted a recommendation to follow antimicrobial use guidelines before treating.

mcqs.q: What did the study find regarding microbiomes and chronic feline URT disease?
o: No microbial features associated with chronic signs
Both gut and nasal microbial members associated with chronic clinical signs
Microbiome was identical to normal cats
mcqs.e: Features within both gut and nasal microbiomes associated with the presence of chronic FURTD signs.

mcqs.q: Where is infectious feline URT disease most prevalent?
o: Wherever cats are housed in groups such as shelters
In cats kept strictly indoors alone
mcqs.e: Its highly transmissible nature makes FURTD most prevalent where cats are group-housed, like shelters.
